Today in 5 minutes

LOUISIANA · 19:54 UTC

Two Louisiana brothers raised 1.7 million dollars for Hamas through a social media scam that solicited donations for the poor and orphans in Gaza, the army blamed Muslims

U.S. law gives the Department of Justice power to charge anyone inside the country who sends money or goods to a group the secretary of state has listed as a foreign terrorist organization. Hamas has held that designation since 1997. Federal prosecutors in Louisiana brought the first charges in the case years ago and kept adding defendants as they traced the money across borders.
On October 2 2026 prosecutors unsealed against Saleem Alzaq, a Gaza resident listed as a deputy commander in Hamas’s Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, and Raed Yusuf of Florida. The same day French internal security officers arrested three men in France identified as Alzaq’s associates. The indictments state that since at least 2020 Alzaq ran Telegram Snapchat and PayPal channels that collected 1.75 million dollars for Hamas 626 000 dollars of it from donors inside the United States. The money was solicited as aid for Gaza but was routed to the group according to the charging documents.
The arrests broke the network that moved the funds and stopped the accounts that hid the destination from payment processors. The case now rests on the evidence in the unsealed and on whether the remaining defendants can be brought to trial in the United States.
